updatesErrorDatabaseHealth: The local database did not become healthy within the limited startup check, or its process failed. The update remains fenced and its backup is preserved. Check available memory, disk space and the local database service, then explicitly resume the same transaction or use recovery. Do not edit the journal or start application writers manually.
updatesErrorDatabaseTarget: The database container, image or data directory does not match this installation. No migration or data replacement was started by this check. Preserve the installation and backup; restore the expected owned runtime before resuming. Do not bypass the identity check.
ollamaModelName: Exact model identifier including variant, for example qwen3:0.6b
ollamaModelPullReview: Review the exact variant, download size, license and resource estimate. This operation changes the explicitly selected local Ollama instance. Free capacity of an externally managed model directory is unknown. An interrupted download can be explicitly repeated using Ollama's partial cache. No inference or cloud processing is activated.
ollamaModelRemoveReview: Remove this single model from the selected local Ollama instance? Check its name and digest. Other applications may use it. The runtime, configuration and other models are not selected for removal. A loaded model must first be deliberately stopped outside this operation.
ollamaModelError: The model operation could not be confirmed. Inspect its saved state with --ollama status. After interruption, explicitly repeat the same operation. Existing tags with a different digest are not overwritten; loaded models are not removed. A changed inventory requires another runtime inspection and selection. Preserve foreign models and settings.
systemToolsError: A required protected system tool is missing or could not be verified. Check the runtime prerequisites.
nativeCryptoScratchError: A short protected GnuPG working directory could not be prepared in the system application folder. Check its path and administrator permissions. No backup password is passed to a process until this check succeeds.
ollamaSelectionReview: Reuse this existing loopback-only Ollama instance? Review its version and models. Kyrion will retain its configuration and services. This selection does not enable inference or cloud processing.
ollamaSelectionResult: Local runtime selected. Its configuration remains under your management. Kyrion AI connection: not connected yet.
ollamaRuntimeError: The local Ollama runtime could not be safely verified. Check that it is running and bound only to loopback addresses. A status or selection does not enable a Kyrion AI connection. You can continue without AI.
publicHttpsTrustError: The public-download certificate trust could not be verified. Repair the system trust store or use an intact signed installer. Explicit certificate settings remain authoritative; do not disable TLS verification.
backupScheduleCryptoRequired: GnuPG and its matching gpgconf are required before enabling backups. On supported Linux targets the OS GnuPG package must be installed; the Windows native bundle supplies the signed support runtime. No backup schedule was enabled by this failed check.
backupScheduleOffer: Configure optional automatic encrypted backups now? You can skip this and use --backup-schedule configure later.
backupScheduleDestination: Absolute path to a dedicated protected backup folder outside the installation (existing parent required)
backupScheduleExport: Absolute path for the separate recovery-key export, outside both installation and backup folder (protected existing parent required)
backupScheduleDays: UTC weekdays, Monday=1 to Sunday=7, separated by commas
backupScheduleClock: Start of the backup window in UTC, HH:MM
backupScheduleDuration: Window duration in minutes, 30 to 1440; already started work can finish later
backupScheduleKeep: Number of verified backups to retain in this store, 1 to 90
backupScheduleReview: Enable a protected background backup task/timer without interactive login. Every fifteen minutes and after boot it checks the selected UTC window. Capture briefly pauses the owned application services, uses the existing consistent encrypted format, then authenticates/decrypts and inspects the result. Up to three interrupted attempts may finish outside the window. Only recorded matching old backups are pruned after a successful backup. Keep the exported key separately and make an independent copy of backups; selecting a path does not verify an off-host copy. No automatic restore or internet connection is enabled.
backupScheduleResetReview: Abandon only the displayed incomplete backup attempt so that settings can be changed or a new capture started. No backup, key or data file is deleted. Any recorded service-recovery obligation remains; inspect services or repair them before assuming availability.
backupScheduleRunReview: Create or resume a configured encrypted backup now, including outside its automatic window. Owned application services may briefly pause. This does not restore data or reset the three-attempt limit.
backupScheduleError: The scheduled backup could not be verified. Check the protected worker, selected UTC window, mounted store marker, available space and key custody. Keep existing backups and the installation journal. Status is available with --backup-schedule status; no restore was started.
backupSchedulePendingError: An incomplete backup retains its three-attempt history. Resume it with --backup-schedule run-now. After inspecting the failure, --backup-schedule reset-incomplete can abandon only that attempt without deleting files, before changing settings or starting a new capture.
updatesErrorResultChanged: The installation changed after this automatic operation finished. Its earlier result is not reported as the current result. Open the current update journal/status and continue that transaction if required; no recovery or new update was started by this check.
linuxServicesReview: Kyrion will install an owned systemd startup service and a protected installer worker. It starts the local Compose project after Docker without an interactive login, uses bounded retries and defers normal startup during unfinished updates or inactive restores. Registration is checked now; physical restart acceptance is a separate check.
startupError: The owned startup service could not be verified. Preserve the installation journal, check systemd, host identity, Docker and worker ownership, then repeat startup configuration. Do not edit ownership or update fences to bypass this check.
identityErrorChanged: This installation already uses a different account issuer or public client. Resume without overriding its saved settings. Existing identity configuration and data are preserved.
updatesPhaseWorking: The saved maintenance operation is running.
updatesPhaseStaging: Verifying and preparing the reviewed program files.
updatesPhasePreparing: Preparing the transaction and stopping application services.
updatesPhaseBackup: Creating and verifying the encrypted backup.
updatesPhaseSwitching: Selecting the verified runtime and configuration.
updatesPhaseMigrating: Running database migrations in maintenance mode.
updatesPhaseChecking: Checking identity, schema and application health.
updatesPhaseRecoveryPreparing: Preparing recovery and stopping application services.
updatesPhaseRecoveryRuntime: Selecting the retained runtime and configuration.
updatesPhaseRecoveryDatabase: Restoring the protected database snapshot and data.
updatesPhaseRecoveryChecking: Checking the restored identity and schema.
updatesPhaseReactivating: Starting and checking the recovered services.
updatesErrorAutomaticAttempts: Automatic continuation stopped after its limited execution attempts, or its retry record is invalid. Backups and the transaction remain preserved. Use the installer as host administrator to inspect the state and explicitly resume or recover with the matching backup password/key. Data is not rewound automatically.
healthErrorWeb: The local login page did not become ready after limited retries. Check the local hostname, HTTPS port and Web/proxy service status, then resume with unchanged inputs. Setup is not marked healthy.
healthErrorTls: The local HTTPS certificate could not be verified. Check the configured hostname and the installation's trusted certificate. Certificate verification remains enabled; do not bypass it.
updatesChannelUnavailable: This development installer has no embedded authenticated release channel. Update scheduling remains unconfigured; no public release availability is implied. Continue local setup normally. An operator can configure a verified channel later.
updatesChannelExisting: Existing update settings are preserved. Use update status, explicit configuration or authenticated trust rotation to manage this installation's channel.
updatesChannelOffer: Recommended: enable notification-only signed update checks after system start and daily. This configures an administrator-protected local worker; it does not install updates automatically. The displayed public trust was embedded by the installer build, not downloaded from the channel. You may skip and continue later.
updatesChannelFailed: The update schedule could not be confirmed. Local Kyrion setup remains usable. The journal retains the concrete failure and any incomplete registration; retry configuration with this installer or inspect update status.
updatesChannelConfigured: The local update-check schedule is registered. This confirms configuration, not a successful cold boot or channel connection. Updates still require explicit installation approval.
updatesErrorSetupRequired: Complete the existing linked account and Space setup before installing updates. No application services have been stopped. Use --continue-setup; do not create a second identity or installation.
updatesErrorAutomatic: Automatic-update approval is missing, changed or outside its UTC start window. Manual transactions and recovery cannot run unattended. Review the signed channel and use --updates automatic to renew consent, or continue the existing transaction manually.
updatesErrorAutomaticKey: The automatic backup key or its protected export did not pass verification. Preserve existing keys and backups; do not generate a replacement for backups already encrypted. Choose an unused export path outside the installation, or retry with the identical earlier export after an interrupted registration.
updatesAutomaticReview: Automatic installation is optional. The approved signed channel may install during your UTC maintenance window, interrupt services and download up to the chosen limit per release. Review the channel's component licenses before enabling. A started transaction may finish or resume after restart outside the window. Recovery that discards newer data is never automatic. A separate administrator-only backup key will be exported: store it outside this computer for disaster recovery. It is not included in backups and will never be printed.
updatesAutomaticDays: UTC weekdays, comma-separated (1 Monday through 7 Sunday)
updatesAutomaticMaximum: Maximum artifact download per release in MiB (1–262144)
updatesAutomaticExport: New protected backup-key export file outside the installation
updatesErrorTransaction: An update is incomplete and ordinary startup remains blocked. Preserve the installation and its backup. Use --updates resume with the same backup password, or --updates recover to review recovery. Do not delete or edit journal flags.
updatesErrorIdentity: Core did not confirm preserved account/Space identities or the protected audit transition. Activation remains blocked. Preserve the encrypted backup and diagnostic state; use the guided recovery path rather than bypassing checks.
updatesErrorRecoveryWrites: Recovery after activation can discard newer application writes. The installer requires a separate acknowledgment and a new encrypted backup of the current state before restoring the pre-update database. No schema downgrade is attempted.
updatesErrorHostUpgrade: The installed or selected runtime lacks the required update-startup fence or Core maintenance protocol. No update was started. Use a compatible signed runtime through the supported repair path first; do not replace individual executable files manually.
updatesApplyReview: Install this verified single-host update. Application services will stop, an encrypted backup and a protected local database snapshot will be created, then the verified runtime and migrations will be checked in maintenance mode. The displayed free-space reserve is an estimate based on current data. Keep the backup passphrase separately; it is needed to resume or recover and is not saved automatically.
updatesResumeReview: Continue the exact previously approved update using its saved journal and verified local inputs. Interrupted migrations may fail again and then require recovery. Application data is not reset after the activation point.
updatesRecoveryReview: Recover this installation's previous runtime. If migration started, restore the validated pre-update database snapshot without a schema downgrade. Failed database contents and changed files are retained. Restored sessions and device credentials are revoked; controls and schedules require review. Keep the backup passphrase available.
updatesRecoveryWrites: The update may already have accepted new writes. Recovery restores older data. A new encrypted backup will first preserve the current data, and the failed database will be retained. Confirm explicitly that post-update writes may be lost from the active installation.
updatesDownloadProgress: Received bytes (integrity verification follows the complete transfer):
updatesErrorDownload: The update download did not finish or the server returned an invalid response. Check the connection and retry the same download; a valid partial file can continue. Existing services have not been updated.
updatesErrorDigest: The downloaded data does not match the authenticated release. It will not be used. Retry only from the configured trusted channel. A corrupted partial artifact is discarded so the next attempt starts cleanly.
updatesErrorChanged: Existing staging data differs from the owned download. It has been preserved. Inspect the protected staging directory before retrying; do not replace installed data to work around this check.
updatesErrorDisk: There is insufficient free space for the remaining download and the operating-system reserve. Free space outside Kyrion's protected data and retry.
updatesErrorCompatibility: The signed candidate, runtime manifest or installed version is incompatible. The existing installation has not been changed. Use a compatible published release and installer.
updatesDownloadReview: Download these authenticated runtime artifacts to private local staging. Sizes are shown below. Interrupted downloads can be retried. Existing services keep running; this action does not install or activate an update.
updatesTrustReview: Apply this trust rotation only if its signature is valid under the installed rotation authority and its epoch is exactly the next one. No release or model is installed by this action.
updatesErrorWorker: Use the independently verified self-contained downloaded installer. Its reviewed executable must remain unchanged while configuring the update worker; a source Python interpreter cannot be installed as that worker.
updatesErrorPolicy: The installed update policy differs. Inspect its status and explicitly disable its owned schedule before configuring another channel or worker. Signed anti-rollback checks remain in force.
updatesErrorSystemd: Automatic Linux checks require a running systemd system manager. This environment cannot install that timer. Manual signed checks remain available; no startup verification is claimed.
updatesScheduleReview: Enable a machine-start and daily signed update check. This copies the self-contained maintenance worker and registers a protected system schedule. Outgoing HTTPS is used. Existing installations keep running when offline. Updates are not installed automatically.
updatesStatus: Update schedule, last attempt and last verified release check (an older successful check is not evidence that the current channel is reachable):
intro: Kyrion local installer. Your setup stays on this target. No AI, microphone, cloud keys or extra hardware is required. This candidate has not passed clean-host release acceptance.
unsupported: E_PLATFORM: This target has no supported provisioning path yet. Windows inventory does not mean Windows installation support. Use an isolated Debian 13 x64/ARM64 or 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS 13 candidate for testing. No system changes were made.
modes: Mode: fresh / resume / repair / restore. Expansion remains separately tracked work.
maintenanceUnavailable: E_MODE: This maintenance operation is not implemented. Existing data is preserved; see docs/guided-installer.md for recovery boundaries.
existing: E_EXISTING_STATE: The target exists. Choose resume for an installation owned by this installer. Existing installations are not adopted or overwritten.
noResume: E_RESUME: No installer journal exists at the target.
trustRequired: E_TRUST: Supply --public-key with an independently trusted release public key. A key downloaded alongside an untrusted bundle is not sufficient.
hostname: Resolvable local hostname, for example kyrion.home.arpa
address: This target's private LAN IPv4 address
review: Review: the four verified images will be loaded; private keys and database configuration are created only for a fresh installation; PostgreSQL, Core, Web and Caddy start. HTTPS binds only to the selected LAN address. No router settings change. Docker Engine must already start as a system service. No additional runtime or model download is performed.
approve: Approve these system changes by typing INSTALL; anything else cancels
working: Preparing runtimes, verifying images and applying approved configuration. Progress is saved; resume with the same target and release after an interruption.
servicesHealthy: Core and local HTTPS login passed the current readiness check. Owner setup and recovery are still separate open steps.
certificate: Public local TLS certificate: trust it through your operating system after verifying its origin. Do not disable TLS verification. It expires after 365 days
handoff: Continue protected owner and Space setup in this installation's local Kyrion interface. Then optionally link the same identity through Profile/Identity and configure integrations through the existing catalog. Website passwords are never entered here. Home Assistant currently imports read-only devices. AI and voice can be skipped.
bootstrap: Read the bootstrap value privately from this protected file, not from logs (Core expiry: 30 minutes)
pending: Installation status and remaining steps are listed below. Optional setup can be continued with this installer; local administration remains available in Kyrion. A recommendation or saved setting alone does not establish successful operation.
interrupted: E_INTERRUPTED: Progress was preserved. Resume the same installation; ambiguous partial files require inspection and are never silently replaced.
failed: Installation could not finish. Existing data and progress are preserved. Check prerequisites, the private install-state.json error code and docs/guided-installer.md, then resume the same release. No automatic deletion or restore was performed.
setupNow: Set up or sign in to your existing local Core account now? You can resume later
spaceName: Name of your new HOME Space (one Space per installation)
localUsername: Local username for the same identity you may link to your web account
localPassword: Local offline password (at least 12 characters; never your website password)
linkNow: Link this local identity to your web account through the configured provider?
linkLater: Central linking is skipped or unavailable. Local access works independently. Later linking uses Profile/Identity; it never creates membership in another Space.
hardwareHelp: Zigbee uses a coordinator; Matter is an application protocol; Thread is an IP network requiring a suitable Border Router. They are not interchangeable. Hardware managed by Home Assistant or another service must stay there; this installer claims no USB device.
hardwareChoice: Select any comma-separated items: ha, zigbee, matter, thread, audio, none. Unknown hardware ownership stays unknown
haExisting: An existing Home Assistant connection is configured. It is preserved. Edit or disconnect it in the local integration catalog.
haScope: Core verifies the connection and imports only your chosen devices and entities. Power control requires separate consent and a deliberate action.
haConsent: Connect Home Assistant with this explicit read-only import scope?
haEndpoint: Home Assistant private IPv4 base URL (http or trusted https)
haToken: Home Assistant access token (stored encrypted by Core, never by this installer)
haImported: Core confirmed connection and imported devices
tutorial: Open Devices to inspect imported states. Only devices declaring control capabilities can be controlled; try an action deliberately. Profile, Space, Integrations and System services remain available after setup.
alreadyLinked: This existing local identity is already linked; the mapping is preserved.
centralBrowser: Open this HTTPS address in your standard browser, verify the provider and sign in or register there. Return here afterward. Do not enter the website password in the installer.
centralCheck: After browser authorization, check the existing Core operation or skip
centralConfirm: Confirm linking the browser-authorized identity to this local account
centralPending: Authorization is still pending. Core enforces the polling interval and expiry.
maintenanceReview: Maintenance affects only the selected local installation. Backup pauses the authoritative Core writer briefly and encrypts data/keys; restore verification starts a new isolated database. Repair preserves original keys; uninstall removes only this installation's containers and keeps data unless separately confirmed. Diagnostics exports only allowlisted metadata, never logs or credentials. Review the selected arguments before continuing
diagnosticSaved: Local diagnostic report saved. Nothing was uploaded.
backupPassword: Backup encryption password (at least 16 characters; store separately from the backup)
deleteDataReview: Permanently remove ALL local data beneath the selected installation directory? Foreign runtimes and files outside that directory are retained
recoveryNow: Set up the existing Core owner recovery now? It pauses Core/Web briefly and requires your current OWNER password
recoveryConsole: The protected Core recovery console will open. Store the one-time offline recovery code separately from the host key and backup. It will not be captured by the installer or included in diagnostics.
haConfigure: Configure or edit Home Assistant now?
haSelectScope: Choose devices and entities. Reading is the default. Home Assistant retains physical pairing; saved consent never switches a device.
haChooseDevices: Device numbers, comma-separated, all or none
haChooseEntities: Entity numbers, comma-separated, all or none
haControlConsent: Allow supported power control for this selected device?
haControlSingle: Power control requires exactly one supported light or switch entity.
haChooseRoom: Keep the matching source room, leave unassigned, or select a room number
haSelectionReview: Save {count} selected devices and their entity, room and control permissions? No physical action occurs.
haFirstAction: Deliberately try one supported power action now?
haChooseActionDevice: Choose exactly one available device number
haActionConfirm: This will physically switch the selected device. Choose the intended action
aiPlanNow: Get local AI model recommendations for this execution device? No download or cloud activation occurs
aiPurpose: Main purpose: everyday assistance, Smart Home or coding
aiPriority: Prioritize speed, quality or lower resource use
aiConcurrent: Device use alongside AI: dedicated, work or gaming
aiBudget: Maximum AI memory budget in whole GiB
aiEstimates: Planning estimates at the stated context size, not measured performance. OS, Kyrion and concurrent use retain reserves. Download bytes are config plus model layers before protocol overhead; existing blobs may reduce the transfer. GPU drivers alone do not prove usable acceleration. No runtime settings have been changed.
aiAlternatives: No suitable recommendation with known resources. Choose another AI device or continue without AI. Cloud processing requires separate explicit consent and is not enabled here.
windowsServicesReview: Native Windows services run at machine startup with separate virtual accounts. Administrator elevation, private runtime copies, loopback PostgreSQL/Core/Web and reviewed local TLS are required. Existing Java, Node, PostgreSQL and Ollama installations are preserved. This candidate is not platform-release approved.
nativeErrorElevation: Start this downloaded installer with administrator rights to install machine services. The system review and confirmation still run before installation.
nativeErrorPort: A required local port is already occupied, or the selected address is unavailable. Resolve the reported conflict deliberately or choose another target device; existing services are preserved.
nativeErrorVersion: This native service candidate requires Windows 11 x64 (build 22000 or later). A candidate is not a platform release approval.
nativeErrorServiceHost: This historical runtime package has no signed native service host. Use a compatible schema-3 service bundle. Verification alone does not install it.
nativeErrorOwnership: The service or installation path does not meet the ownership policy. Review its permissions and identity before continuing; foreign services are not replaced.
centralOpen: Open secure provider login, or check after approving the displayed code in your browser. Cancel leaves account creation pending.
linkedOfflineIdentity: Web identity confirmed. Choose a local username and a separate offline password for this same identity. Never enter your web password here.
spaceAuthorized: Core verified your membership in this installation’s active Space. Other installations require a prepared, authorized device connection.
spaceUse: Use this authorized Space for the remaining setup?
identityAccess: Connect your web account, or use the already linked identity with its local offline password
identityReview: Core identity provider for browser-only sign-in; no website password or shared client secret is stored
offlineIdentityPolicy: Offline access uses this same linked local identity and Core membership rules. Local password sessions expire after seven days. A web-account block prevents new central login; it does not immediately revoke offline access. Local account or membership suspension takes effect through Core checks.
spaceInvitationChoice: This web account has no local membership. LINK an existing local identity, or JOIN this Space with an authorized invitation.
spaceInvitationEmail: Invitation email, if required by this Space (leave blank otherwise)
spaceInvitationEmailProof: Mailbox verification code (requires this installation’s configured mail service)
setupMemberOnly: Your membership is confirmed. Your role does not permit installation administration; an authorized administrator must configure devices and integrations.
linkExistingLocal: This local account has no web link. Explicitly connect this same identity now? Existing membership, roles and password are retained.
bootstrapExtendReview: Extend the protected first-owner setup window for 30 minutes. Available only before an owner exists. Sign-in proofs retain their separate shorter expiry.
identityErrorUnavailable: The identity provider is unavailable. Retry later; an already linked installation can use OFFLINE access. New account setup remains pending.
identityErrorConfiguration: The Core identity provider is disabled or not configured. Configure the reviewed issuer/public client before continuing; no local account has been linked by this error.
identityErrorRestart: Start a fresh sign-in operation and approve its current code. Expired, denied or consumed proofs cannot be reused.
identityErrorBootstrap: The protected first-owner credential is missing, invalid or expired. For an unfinished owned installation use --continue-setup or --extend-bootstrap with host administrator rights.
identityErrorExistingOwner: This installation already has, or is expected to have, an owner. Use the existing local identity or its recovery path; first-owner setup is unavailable.
identityErrorMembership: Sign-in alone does not grant Space access. LINK an existing local account or JOIN using an authorized Space invitation.
identityErrorInvitation: The invitation or required mailbox proof could not be redeemed. Check its expiry, remaining uses, email restriction and the issuing Space before requesting a new proof.
identityErrorLinked: This identity is already linked. Use the existing linked account; this operation does not replace a link or merge users.
identityErrorLocalAccess: Local authentication failed or the session ended. Sign in again with the local offline password, or use the consciously configured host recovery path.
identityErrorRateLimit: Core has limited repeated authentication attempts. Wait before retrying; further failed attempts can increase the delay.
identityErrorPermission: Your current role does not authorize this action. Ask a Space administrator to perform or explicitly grant the required operation.
identityErrorPasswordMismatch: The local offline passwords do not match. Restart the credential step; no password is stored by the installer.
identitySetupPaused: Account/Space setup is paused. Continue with --continue-setup on this installation; confirmed Core changes and local progress remain available.
recoveryMaintenanceReview: This host-console operation briefly stops Core and Web, leaving the database running. Core requests secrets privately. Open consumes the recovery code; complete changes the OWNER password and revokes sessions; rotate invalidates previous recovery codes. Keep newly displayed codes privately.
haImportRoomReview: Import this Home Assistant area as a Kyrion room now? Existing rooms with the same name are reused; no physical devices are paired or controlled. Room creation remains saved if you later cancel device selection.
haDisconnectReview: Disconnect Home Assistant from this Space and remove its stored token and device selection? Home Assistant itself, physical pairings and other integrations remain unchanged.
maintenanceErrorRuntime: This installation lacks the verified backup runtime. Repair or extend it with a compatible signed runtime bundle before creating a backup. Existing data stays in place.
maintenanceErrorServices: A service could not be restarted after backup capture. The installer retained its restart obligation. Resolve the platform service or container error and run backup maintenance again; no successful backup is reported for this attempt.
updateErrorIndex: The update index conflicts with the last verified index or uses an older trust epoch. Keep the installed version and obtain a corrected signed channel/trust configuration from the release maintainer.
updateErrorSchema: The installed database schema could not be verified or does not match the requested compatibility check. Check the local PostgreSQL service and installation integrity before retrying.
updateErrorDevelopment: This development installer cannot query a stable update channel as a released installer. Use isolated signed-channel tests until a supported installer is explicitly released.
restoreRetireReview: This permanently retires this source installation for the displayed backup and target. Kyrion services are stopped and disabled/removed. Ordinary repair or startup will refuse this authority. Export the transfer receipt and keep the original backup; an offline source without a retirement receipt cannot enable a competing restored writer.
restoreReview: Restore creates or resumes only the displayed prepared target using the verified runtime bundle. It requires a portable backup with matching release/schema and source retirement. Original account/Space data and application keys are restored; host configuration is newly generated. Old sessions/device credentials are revoked; queued actions and HA control are not replayed. It does not merge with existing data or perform schema downgrade.
restoreAwaitingRetirement: Target prepared and inactive. Run --retire-for-restore on the source installer with this backup, the displayed --restore-target-id and --transfer-receipt OUTPUT. Then repeat --restore on this target with --transfer-receipt INPUT. No activation occurs without a valid matching receipt.
restoreReviewRequired: Restore activation completed. Re-enrol gateway/voice devices, review Home Assistant control, re-enable calendar schedules consciously and rotate owner recovery codes. Use the existing local account password; old sessions are invalid.
restoreBackupPath: Path to the encrypted portable backup
restoreReceiptPath: Transfer receipt path; leave empty to prepare the inactive target first
restoreErrorCompatibility: This restore path requires portable table data, PostgreSQL 17, Core schema 49 and a matching signed runtime bundle with the local Core restore tool. Migration checksums and schema must match. Legacy SQL-only dumps are not executed on the application target. Create a new capture from a compatible source if needed. The target remains inactive after an unsuccessful import.
restoreErrorAudit: Core did not confirm the transfer proof, existing audit chain or security disposition. The target is not activated. Preserve the backup and diagnostic state and check original keys, receipt and compatible Core version; do not bypass security checks.
restoreErrorGuardUpgrade: The source lacks the verified retirement guard. Upgrade its installer runtime through a supported signed path first. Do not edit journal flags manually. No transfer receipt was issued.
restoreErrorInactive: This installation is retired or prepared as an inactive restore target. Ordinary repair/start must not activate it. Continue only the same displayed transfer with the same backup and target ID.
restoreErrorReceipt: The transfer receipt is missing or does not match the source, target and backup. Generate it with --retire-for-restore on the supported source and transfer only the receipt file. An offline source that has not been safely retired cannot authorize target activation.
restoreErrorTarget: The target contains existing/unexpectedly changed data or belongs to another restore request. Data is preserved. Inspect the saved operation and use only the originally reviewed backup; do not overwrite unexplained changes.
maintenancePaused: Maintenance was interrupted. Checkpointed steps remain available; resume the same operation with unchanged verified inputs. A prepared restore target is not activated automatically.
installDownloadReview: Download the authenticated published platform bundle. Review its components, exact download size and release notes below. System installation requires a separate confirmation afterwards. Known partial downloads are resumed; the cache is retained.
installDownloadChannelRequired: This development build has no embedded authenticated release channel. No public runtime download is available through it. Use an operator-provided signed bundle with its independently trusted key, or a released installer with a configured channel.
installDownloadError: The selected release or protected download cache could not be verified. No installation was started. Preserve the cache and use a compatible signed release; do not replace its proof, marker or files manually.
cryptoPackageReview: Optional Linux backup prerequisite: refresh metadata from your existing package sources, then review exact GnuPG package versions and download/installed sizes before separate installation consent. No repository, key, existing package upgrade or removal is permitted. Package downloads remain subject to APT authentication. Raw package-manager output is kept out of the installer journal.
cryptoPackageError: An OS package prerequisite could not be verified or completed. Guided package installation supports Debian 13 only. No OS-wide repair, existing-package upgrade/removal or authentication bypass is performed. Preserve the journal and package state. Retry cryptography with --install-crypto, or select Resume for the approved runtime installation. Unrelated incomplete package work requires the system administrator.
linuxRuntimeReview: Linux runtime prerequisite: review exact package versions and allocation before installing Docker Engine, Compose v2 and GnuPG from existing authenticated Debian sources. Package maintainer scripts may start/enable Docker, so service consent is requested first. Existing containers may resume according to their own policies. No daemon configuration, group membership or LAN TCP API is added; shared runtimes are retained on Kyrion removal. Actual system boot remains separately unverified.
linuxRuntimeError: The supported local Linux runtime could not be prepared or verified. This guided package path targets Debian 13 with systemd and the standard packaged local rootful Docker service. Existing custom tools, daemon data, masks and service overrides are preserved. Use a compatible prepared local service or another supported target; do not remove foreign data or disable security checks. Resume the installer for an interrupted approved runtime operation.
nativeBackupVerificationReview: Verification creates an inactive temporary database on this installation's verified local PostgreSQL server, imports the backup and checks its schema, constraints and counts. It needs additional disk space. The live database is not replaced and application services are not started. A prior unacknowledged database creation requires review before cleanup.
nativeBackupVerificationError: Backup database verification could not finish. Keep the archive and installation journal. This path needs an installed compatible signed Core runtime and its verified local PostgreSQL. An unacknowledged or replaced temporary database is preserved for administrator review; never delete a database based on its name alone. The live database has not been selected as a restore target.
devicesScope: Manage paired devices in this Space. This does not move the Kyrion central installation. Intermittent devices cannot provide their functions while switched off.
devicesEmpty: No paired devices. Choose PAIR to create a transfer for the installer on the other device.
devicesSelect: Select device number, PAIR for another device, or 0 to finish
devicesRevoked: This device is revoked. Its previous access cannot be restored; a new authorized enrollment is required.
devicesAction: Edit name/availability, task permissions, or revoke device access
devicesAvailability: Expected availability (unknown / always on / intermittently on)
devicesRemoveReview: Revoke this device and its linked voice access, and fail outstanding commands? Already delivered physical actions cannot be recalled. Local software and user data are retained.
devicesReadBack: Request accepted. Reading current device state from Core.
devicesTasksScope: These task permissions control existing gateway integrations and linked voice access in Core. They do not install or start software or microphones. Reported services are last-known agent observations; offline reports are not proof of readiness. Distributed AI and central migration require their own supported setup.
devicesTasksChoice: Allow integration and/or voice, or choose none
devicesTasksReview: Apply the displayed task permissions? Removing integration fails outstanding commands; removing voice ends linked sessions. Software, hardware configuration and data are retained.
nodeForegroundScope: Prepared Linux node: use the existing protected gateway identity over verified local TLS. These foreground operations do not install services or start recording.
nodePairReview: Compare the displayed certificate fingerprint with your Kyrion central installation before pairing. The code file is short-lived and used once; its contents are not displayed. PAIR saves protected credentials. With no connection arguments, resume the existing pending operation.
nodePaired: Core confirmed the device identity. Task permissions must be assigned in the central device management; enrollment alone is not a running service.
nodeHeartbeatReview: Send one real device health/inventory report to the paired central installation? No command polling, microphone capture or device-control test is started.
nodeRunReview: Run this prepared node in the foreground until Ctrl+C? It requests current task permissions from Core before integration polling and event forwarding. Authorized Core commands may control configured devices. Connection loss or expired permissions stop local task activity; revoked access stops the runtime. No microphone recording, operating-system service installation or automatic startup is activated.
nodeRuntimeBusy: Another local runtime already holds this prepared-device configuration. Stop that foreground process or the owned service before starting another instance. Preserve the configuration and lock file; do not copy the credentials to another device.
nodeAccessDenied: Core rejected this device access. Local task activity has stopped. Check the device and Space status in the central installation. A revoked identity requires an explicitly authorized new enrollment; do not overwrite the saved credentials automatically.
nodePolicyUnavailable: The central task policy is unavailable or cannot be verified. No legacy authority is assumed. Check central version, local TLS routing and device configuration, then explicitly resume with the saved identity. Do not disable certificate verification.
nodeTrustInvalid: The confirmed or stored device certificate cannot be verified. Compare its fingerprint with the central installation through a trusted local channel. Preserve the pending identity and credentials and correct the trust configuration deliberately. Do not disable TLS verification.
nodeServiceReview: The installer configures a system service with a dedicated non-login Linux account. Only the protected agent directory is writable; direct USB and microphone access is blocked. The service starts at system startup without user login. Removal stops and removes the service; device identity, credentials and technical account are retained. This does not revoke pairing in Core.
nodeServiceError: Node service setup could not be verified. Keep the existing installation directory. Check systemd availability, the recorded technical account and owned unit/worker permissions, then resume with the same target. Changed or foreign service definitions are preserved for inspection. Core device removal is separate.
nodePairingExportScope: Run the downloaded installer on the other device. This creates a ten-minute, one-use pairing file for this Space, not a remote installation. Transfer it privately and compare the certificate fingerprint on both devices. It contains a temporary secret; do not publish or upload it.
nodePairingExportReview: Check the actual local TLS agent connection and create a pairing transfer?
nodePairingExportSaved: Pairing file saved privately. On the target select it with --node-pairing. Successful source-side connection does not prove target DNS or network reachability. Delete the transfer after use; expiry is enforced by Core.
nodePairingImportReview: Compare this certificate fingerprint and Space with the originating installer before pairing. The target verifies its own local TLS connection. This transfer grants no permission to replace an existing identity.
nodePairingError: The pairing transfer could not be verified. Check its private file permissions, the system clock, expiry and the originating certificate fingerprint. A pending installation can resume without re-importing an expired transfer. Do not disable TLS verification.
nodePairingIngressRequired: The configured HTTPS listener does not provide the prepared-agent route. A reviewed extension of the managed local proxy and a compatible Core are required before a pairing file can be issued. Existing proxy configuration was preserved.
agentIngressScope: Extend only the recorded local proxy for authenticated device communication. The existing TLS address stays the same; no ports, router rules or downloads are added. Local web/device access is briefly interrupted while only the proxy restarts. Custom configurations are preserved. Recovery restores the recorded original configuration; verified TLS alone does not prove all components healthy.
agentIngressError: The proxy transition is incomplete or could not be verified. Preserve the installation. Use --agent-ingress status, then resume with an authorized linked account or explicitly recover the recorded original configuration. Ordinary startup and updates remain fenced while the transition is incomplete. No keys or application data were replaced.
agentIngressWorkerUpgrade: An enabled installed startup, update or backup worker cannot honor the proxy transition fence. Before retrying, upgrade that owned worker with this current installer using its existing autostart, update or backup configuration. Source changes alone do not replace scheduled executables. No proxy change was made.
agentIngressPlatform: This managed proxy transition is currently implemented for Linux Compose. The native Windows transition adapter is not implemented yet. Existing configuration is preserved.
